claims.title: Massinissa unites Numidia
claims.summary: Allied with Rome in the Second Punic War, the Massylian king Massinissa defeats Syphax and unifies the Amazigh kingdom of Numidia, ruling until 148 BCE.

sources.label: Berber Kingdoms of Numidia and Mauretania

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-202bce-massinissa-unites-numidia, claim TL:DZA:event:202bce:massinissa-unites-numidia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Jugurthine War
claims.summary: Massinissa's grandson Jugurtha wars with Rome over control of Numidia; captured by treachery, he is led in Marius's triumph and executed at Rome in 104 BCE.

sources.label: Berber Kingdoms of Numidia and Mauretania

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-112bce-the-jugurthine-war, claim TL:DZA:event:112bce:the-jugurthine-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Trajan founds Timgad
claims.summary: The emperor Trajan establishes Timgad (Thamugadi) as a Roman colony; its grid plan, forum, theatre and arch survive as one of the best-preserved Roman towns.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-100-trajan-founds-timgad, claim TL:DZA:event:100:trajan-founds-timgad, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Augustine, bishop of Hippo
claims.summary: Augustine serves as bishop of Hippo Regius from about 395 until his death in 430, writing the Confessions and City of God and shaping Western Christian thought.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-396-augustine-bishop-of-hippo, claim TL:DZA:event:396:augustine-bishop-of-hippo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Vandals take Carthage
claims.summary: After seizing Hippo Regius, Genseric's Vandals capture Carthage in 439 and rule a kingdom commanding the western Mediterranean.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-439-vandals-take-carthage, claim TL:DZA:event:439:vandals-take-carthage, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Byzantine reconquest
claims.summary: Justinian's general Belisarius lands in 533 and within a year destroys the Vandal kingdom, restoring Byzantine imperial rule over coastal North Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-533-byzantine-reconquest, claim TL:DZA:event:533:byzantine-reconquest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kusaila defeats Uqba ibn Nafi
claims.summary: The Awraba chief Kusaila ambushes and kills the Arab general Uqba ibn Nafi near Biskra, a high point of Amazigh resistance to the Islamic conquest.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-683-kusaila-defeats-uqba-ibn-nafi, claim TL:DZA:event:683:kusaila-defeats-uqba-ibn-nafi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Kahina and the fall of Carthage
claims.summary: The Amazigh queen known as the Kahina leads resistance from the Aurès before her defeat around 698, the year the Arabs take Carthage and end Byzantine rule in Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-698-the-kahina-and-the-fall-of-carthage, claim TL:DZA:event:698:the-kahina-and-the-fall-of-carthage, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hammadid dynasty and Beni Hammad
claims.summary: The Berber Hammadid dynasty is established and founds the Qal'a of Beni Hammad; Bejaïa becomes one of the foremost ports of North Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1011-hammadid-dynasty-and-beni-hammad, claim TL:DZA:event:1011:hammadid-dynasty-and-beni-hammad, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Barbarossa brothers seize Algiers
claims.summary: The corsair Aruj takes Algiers; his brother Hayreddin places it under Ottoman suzerainty, founding the Regency of Algiers.

sources.label: From Pirate to Admiral: The Tale of Barbarossa

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1516-barbarossa-brothers-seize-algiers, claim TL:DZA:event:1516:barbarossa-brothers-seize-algiers, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman suzerainty established
claims.summary: After Aruj's death, Hayreddin Barbarossa submits Algiers to the Ottoman sultan and is made beylerbey, binding the regency to Istanbul.

sources.label: From Pirate to Admiral: The Tale of Barbarossa

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1518-ottoman-suzerainty-established, claim TL:DZA:event:1518:ottoman-suzerainty-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rule of the deys
claims.summary: Power in the regency passes to elected military rulers titled dey, heading a janissary state financed by corsairing and ransom.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1671-rule-of-the-deys, claim TL:DZA:event:1671:rule-of-the-deys, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The "fly-whisk" incident
claims.summary: A dispute over French debts ends with the dey of Algiers striking the French consul with a fly-whisk, a slight France later uses as a pretext for invasion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1827-the-fly-whisk-incident, claim TL:DZA:event:1827:the-fly-whisk-incident, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France captures Algiers
claims.summary: A French expeditionary force takes Algiers, ending the Ottoman regency and beginning 132 years of French rule in Algeria.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1830-france-captures-algiers, claim TL:DZA:event:1830:france-captures-algiers, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abd al-Qadir's resistance
claims.summary: Proclaimed amir in 1832, Abd al-Qadir builds a state across much of Algeria and leads armed resistance to the French until his surrender in 1847.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1832-abd-al-qadir-s-resistance, claim TL:DZA:event:1832:abd-al-qadir-s-resistance, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Algeria annexed to France
claims.summary: Algeria is organised into French départements and declared an integral part of France, opening the way to large-scale European settlement and land expropriation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1848-algeria-annexed-to-france, claim TL:DZA:event:1848:algeria-annexed-to-france, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Mokrani (Kabyle) revolt
claims.summary: A major uprising in Kabylia is crushed, followed by further confiscations of land that deepen the dispossession of the Muslim population.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1871-the-mokrani-kabyle-revolt, claim TL:DZA:event:1871:the-mokrani-kabyle-revolt, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sétif massacre
claims.summary: A nationalist demonstration at Sétif on VE Day is met with mass killing of thousands of Algerians, radicalising the independence movement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1945-setif-massacre, claim TL:DZA:event:1945:setif-massacre, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Toussaint Rouge: the war begins
claims.summary: The FLN launches coordinated attacks across Algeria on 1 November 1954, opening the war of independence against French rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1954-toussaint-rouge-the-war-begins, claim TL:DZA:event:1954:toussaint-rouge-the-war-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Algiers
claims.summary: A fierce urban campaign in the capital pits FLN cells against French paratroopers; the army's use of torture turns world opinion against the war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1956-battle-of-algiers, claim TL:DZA:event:1956:battle-of-algiers, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The war topples the Fourth Republic
claims.summary: The Algerian crisis brings down France's Fourth Republic and returns Charles de Gaulle to power, opening the way to eventual negotiations.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1958-the-war-topples-the-fourth-republic, claim TL:DZA:event:1958:the-war-topples-the-fourth-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Évian Accords
claims.summary: France and the FLN sign the Évian Accords, agreeing a ceasefire and a self-determination referendum that will lead to Algerian independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1962-evian-accords, claim TL:DZA:event:1962:evian-accords, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence proclaimed
claims.summary: After a referendum on 1 July and French recognition on 3 July, Algeria proclaims its independence on 5 July 1962, ending 132 years of French rule.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Algeria
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1962-independence-proclaimed, claim TL:DZA:event:1962:independence-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Boumédiène seizes power
claims.summary: Colonel Houari Boumédiène overthrows Ahmed Ben Bella and installs himself as president, beginning thirteen years of centralised socialist rule.

sources.label: Boumédienne Seizes Power from Dictator in Algeria

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1965-boumediene-seizes-power, claim TL:DZA:event:1965:boumediene-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Nationalisation of oil and gas
claims.summary: Boumédiène nationalises the hydrocarbon industry, using oil and gas revenues to fund state-led industrialisation and a socialist development model.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1971-nationalisation-of-oil-and-gas, claim TL:DZA:event:1971:nationalisation-of-oil-and-gas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Elections cancelled; civil war begins
claims.summary: After the Islamic Salvation Front leads the December 1991 vote, the army cancels the elections and ousts the president, triggering the civil war of the 1990s.

sources.label: Algeria: Civil war—the Islamists versus the army

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1992-elections-cancelled-civil-war-begins, claim TL:DZA:event:1992:elections-cancelled-civil-war-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bouteflika and national reconciliation
claims.summary: Elected in 1999, Abdelaziz Bouteflika ends the civil war through a Civil Concord and the 2005 Charter for Peace and National Reconciliation.

sources.label: Algeria: Civil war—the Islamists versus the army

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-1999-bouteflika-and-national-reconciliation, claim TL:DZA:event:1999:bouteflika-and-national-reconciliation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Hirak and Bouteflika's fall
claims.summary: Mass peaceful protests known as the Hirak erupt against Bouteflika's bid for a fifth term; he resigns on 2 April 2019, and Abdelmadjid Tebboune is elected president that December.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Algeria: From Numidian kings and Roman Hippo to the war of independence and the Hirak.", terralore.co/country/DZA/chronicle#ev-2019-the-hirak-and-bouteflika-s-fall, claim TL:DZA:event:2019:the-hirak-and-bouteflika-s-fall, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
